articles.title: Boris Vujčić: Risks and resilience in the euro area financial system
articles.excerpt:
It is my great pleasure to open this year's Frankfurt Euro Finance Week. This event provides a timely opportunity to reflect on the state of the euro area financial system and the challenges ahead. It also comes just two days before the ECB publishes its latest Financial Stability Review (FSR). My key message today is that Europe needs more market-based finance. At the same time, however, a larger role for non-banks must go hand in hand with stronger system-wide safeguards.

articles.title: Yen steady against euro and dollar after soft Japanese GDP data
articles.excerpt:
SINGAPORE, Nov 16 (Reuters) - The yen was pinned near two-month lows against the dollar and little moved against the euro in early trade on Monday as markets assessed how an unexpected contraction in the Japanese economy in the third quarter affects the policy outlook.

The yen fluctuated between gains and losses without moving too far, trading against the dollar at 159.69 yen and against the euro at 176.04 yen, close to levels where US and Japanese authorities are believed to have intervened earlier this year.

articles.title: Rupee rises, volatility ebbs as equity inflows blunt global headwinds
articles.excerpt:
The Indian rupee demonstrated notable strength by closing 0.3% higher at 93.9225 against the dollar. November saw foreign equity inflows amounting to nearly $10 billion, reversing recent trends of outflows. Analysts highlighted that these inflows contributed to the rupee's stabilization amid expectations of potential US interest rate hikes. The Nifty 50 index also climbed by 0.6%, buoyed by limited exposure to AI trades.

articles.title: Morgan Stanley sees Sensex at 1.05 lakh in bull case by December 2027; base target at 95,000
articles.excerpt:
Morgan Stanley’s latest base case assumes robust domestic growth, steady global growth, a resolution of the India-US trade deal and Brent crude below $100 a barrel.

Morgan Stanley has pegged the BSE Sensex at 95,000 by December 2027 in its base-case scenario, implying an upside of 16 per cent from its November 12, 2026 reference level of 81,911. In its bull-case scenario, the brokerage sees the benchmark rising to 1,05,000, while its bear case places the index at 68,000.

The base case carries a 50 per cent probability, while the bull and bear scenarios have probabilities of 30 per cent and 20 per cent, respectively. The probability-weighted outcome is 90,750.
